tasks.short: Keep storage areas and carts stocked, clean and tidy.

steps.what: Check storage areas and carts for what is missing.
Rewrite a shortfall list for those storage areas.
Clean the storage areas and wipe the carts.
Restock carts until each line is stocked and tidy.

tasks.design: The cleaner still checks the storage areas, cleans them and restocks the carts by hand. A paper par card fixed to each cart replaces the fresh shortfall list, so that rewrite drops out. No system is added: the cleaner stocks from the card and from what they see.
tasks.previous_blocker: The shortfall lived on a new handwritten list, and the cart itself did not show a stable par. Nearly all of this work is standing in the storage area, so there was no screen to configure.
tasks.enabler_now: A printed par card needs no interface. The cleaner already knows the lines that belong on the cart.
tasks.still_hard: Telling a stained item from a short one, and leaving a cart tidy in a tight closet, is still the cleaner's eye and hands. A card does not clean or lift.
tasks.human_edge: The cleaner sees dirt, damage and a gap that a fixed par line does not describe, and decides what tidy means for that closet.

ambition.what: Restock a cart that sits below the par card before starting the next floor.

tasks.altitude: The round is still walking, cleaning and stocking. The week loses the rewritten shortfall list. The cleaner still decides when a cart is tidy enough to take out.

reach.task: See which carts were below par without asking for a recopied list
reach.learn: The card shows the lines. The cleaner still has to say what was actually short or dirty.

evidence.claim: A fixed par on paper can replace a fresh handwritten shortfall list. It does not clean a closet or stock a cart.
Stock lines for linen and cleaning items are not personal data. A par card does not need a consent step unless it starts recording who stocked the cart.

assumptions: The focal boundary is the cleaner checking, cleaning and stocking. The par card is paper. There is no stock system in this task.
The rewritten list is the small paper slice. Only that step goes. Cleaning and stocking stay at full time.
Par-card upkeep, when a line changes, is half an hour per 100 baseline hours of this task, and it is not already inside a step.
If a site has no list today, the saving is about zero. That is the low end of the range.
unknowns: Whether carts already carry a par card.
How often the par lines change, and who is allowed to change them.
research_questions: What share of shifts starts by rewriting a shortfall list?
Which cart lines run out mid-floor even when the morning par was met?

already_counted.description: Time still spent checking storage areas, cleaning them and stocking carts.

incremental.description: Reprint or amend the cart par card when a stock line changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Checking, cleaning and stocking stay. Only the rewritten shortfall list goes, and par-card upkeep is taken off. The low end is a site with no list today. The high end is several carts whose lists are rewritten each shift. Both sit under the central net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Replenish glasses, linens, writing supplies and bathroom items.

steps.what: See which drinking glasses and linens the room lacks.
Rewrite the supplies list for this room.
Replenish supplies of linens and drinking glasses.
Replenish writing supplies and bathroom items.

tasks.design: The cleaner still looks at the room and places drinking glasses, linens, writing supplies and bathroom items by hand, including rejecting a chipped glass or a stained linen. A paper amenity card for the room type, carried on the cart, replaces the rewritten supplies list. The card does not place anything.
tasks.previous_blocker: The standard set lived in memory or on a list rewritten per room. Room types differ, and a chipped glass is a look, not a code.
tasks.enabler_now: Room types are few and stable enough to print one amenity card per type. The cleaner already carries the cart into the room.
tasks.still_hard: A card cannot see a cracked glass, a missing towel behind a door, or a room that was sold as a different type overnight.
tasks.human_edge: The cleaner rejects items a guest should not receive, and places them where that room actually needs them.

ambition.what: Read the room-type card before placing supplies in a room that is not the standard set.

tasks.altitude: The cleaner still replenishes every room on the board. The rewritten supplies list drops. They still decide a chipped glass or a short linen set before the guest returns.

reach.task: Set the amenity card when a room type changes
reach.learn: The card is the standard set. Exceptions still come from the cleaner in the room.

evidence.claim: A printed room-type list can replace a list rewritten in each room. Placing glasses, linens and bathroom items stays manual.
Amenity counts for a room type are not personal data, unless the card starts naming the guest or the cleaner as a score.

assumptions: The focal boundary is looking and placing in the guest room. The amenity card is paper. Nothing is ordered from a supplier in this task.
Placing items where a guest will use them is an external effect, so those steps are marked act_external. They stay fully manual.
Only the rewritten supplies list is removed. Card upkeep when a room type changes is half an hour per 100 baseline hours.
A site that never writes a supplies list saves about nothing. That is the low end.
unknowns: How many room types the site actually uses, and how often a room is sold as a different type.
Who refills the central cupboard the cart is stocked from.
research_questions: How often a room is left short of glasses, linens or bathroom items after the cleaner has left?
How often the cleaner rejects an item that the standard set would still have placed?

already_counted.description: Time still spent seeing gaps and placing glasses, linens, writing supplies and bathroom items.

incremental.description: Amend the room-type amenity card when the standard set changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Looking and placing stay, including the rejection of a bad glass or linen. Only the rewritten supplies list goes, and card upkeep is taken off. The low end is a site with no list. The high end is a board of rooms whose lists are rewritten today. Both sit under the central net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Report damage, theft and found articles after protecting guest property.

steps.what: Observe precautions required to protect hotel and guest property.
Note damage, theft and found articles in the room.
Copy that room note into a second report for supervisors.
Tell the supervisors what the report says.
Supervisors accept the report of damage, theft and found articles.
File the accepted report on the property log.

tasks.design: The cleaner still observes the room and writes damage, theft or a found article once on the room note. That note is the report, so the second copy is dropped, and the cleaner still tells the supervisor in person. The housekeeping supervisor accepts the note before it is filed in {DOCS}. The file states what was seen, and a person still decides whether it is damage, theft or a found article.
tasks.previous_blocker: The room note was copied out again for the supervisor, and a later log could drift from what was said. Calling an item theft is a judgement with legal weight, so it could not be a rule on a form.
tasks.enabler_now: One room note can be the report the supervisor accepts, and a document store can file that accepted note against the room and the shift.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing the difference between wear, damage, a lost item and a possible theft happens in the room. A form cannot make that call, and a wrong word is hard to undo.
tasks.human_edge: The cleaner sees the room and chooses words for what they saw. The supervisor accepts the report before anyone else relies on it.

ambition.what: Put a found-article note with the supervisor before the room is prepared for the next guest.

tasks.altitude: Watching the room and writing the note stay the bulk of the task. The second copy and the recopying into the log drop where the log is already a document store. The supervisor still accepts the report, and still decides what it means.

reach.task: Act on one accepted note of damage, theft or a found article
reach.learn: The note is what the cleaner saw, tied to the room and the shift. It is not a finding that a crime occurred.

evidence.claim: Filing an already accepted note in a document store is ordinary records configuration. It does not decide whether an event is damage, theft or a found article.

A note that names a guest, or describes a belonging that identifies them, is personal data under the GDPR. Access belongs with the people who handle lost property, and national lost-property rules vary.
A log that names the cleaner and is later used to compare staff is staff monitoring. Works-council consent comes before that use. The log in this design is not a score.

assumptions: The focal boundary is observing, writing the room note, telling the supervisor and filing. The supervisor's acceptance is other-role time and is not sped up.
The room note is the report. The second copy is the step that is removed. The spoken report stays.
The file stores room, shift, the cleaner's words and the supervisor's acceptance. It does not store a theft classification made by software. A later edit voids the acceptance.
Form upkeep when rooms are renumbered is 0.6 hour per 100 baseline hours of this task.
If the site has no document store, filing stays by hand and only the second copy drops. That is why the low end is well under the central net.
unknowns: Whether found-article notes today include a guest name.
Which national lost-property rule applies, and how long the site already keeps these notes.
Whether a supervisor already accepts every note, or only theft and high-value finds.
research_questions: What share of these events is a found article, against damage, against a suspected theft?
How often the log text differs from the room note the cleaner wrote?

already_counted.description: Time still spent observing, writing the room note and telling the supervisor.

incremental.description: Keep the report form matched to the room list when rooms are renumbered.

approvals.approved_version: Room note of damage, theft or found articles for this room and shift, as the housekeeping supervisor accepted. A later change voids the acceptance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Observing, writing the room note and telling the supervisor stay. The supervisor's acceptance stays and is not the cleaner's time. The low end is a site that still writes the log by hand, so only the second copy drops and form upkeep eats most of it. The high end is a site that already files housekeeping notes in the document store, so the copy and the recopying into the log both drop. Both sit under the central net, which prices the log as configured and subtracts form upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Sort, count and mark clean linens and store them in closets.

steps.what: Sort clean linens by size in the linen room.
Count clean linens and mark rejects by hand.
Rewrite the linen count for the closets.
Store accepted linens in the linen closets.

tasks.design: The cleaner still sorts, counts, marks and stores clean linens in the linen closets by hand. A paper par card on the closet replaces the rewritten count sheet, so the count is kept once, on the card, while the linen is handled. Stained or torn linen is still marked out by the cleaner before it is stored.
tasks.previous_blocker: The count was rewritten onto a fresh sheet after the linen was already in the cleaner's hands. Stains and tears are visible only at the pile, and the closet has no screen.
tasks.enabler_now: A closet par card can take the count in one writing. The types of linen are stable enough to print.
tasks.still_hard: Sorting by size, feeling a thin sheet, and marking a reject are physical. A card does not move linen or see a stain.
tasks.human_edge: The cleaner marks linen that should not go back to a room, and stacks a closet so the next cart can be loaded.

ambition.what: Set aside a linen type that is already over the closet par before taking more from the laundry.

tasks.altitude: Sorting, counting, marking and storing stay the work. The rewritten count sheet drops. The cleaner still decides which pieces are rejected before they enter the closet.

reach.task: Deliver the next clean linen against what the closet still needs
reach.learn: The par card shows the count the cleaner wrote while sorting. It does not replace a look at stains.

evidence.claim: Writing a count once on a closet card can replace a second handwritten count sheet. Sorting, marking and storing linen stay manual.
Linen counts are not personal data unless the card is used to time or rank the person who counted.

assumptions: The focal boundary is sorting, counting, marking and storing. The par card is paper. There is no linen system in this task.
Only the rewritten count sheet is removed. Sorting, counting, marking rejects and carrying linen to the closet stay at full time.
Amending the closet par when the mix of linen changes is 0.4 hour per 100 baseline hours, and it is not already inside a step.
A site that never rewrites a count saves about nothing. That is the low end.
unknowns: Whether the closet is counted at all today, or only sorted and stacked.
Who sets the par, the cleaner or the laundry.
research_questions: What share of clean linen is marked reject before it is stored?
How often a closet runs out of one type while another type is over par?

already_counted.description: Time still spent sorting, counting, marking and storing clean linens.

incremental.description: Amend the closet par card when the mix of linen types changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Sorting, counting, marking rejects and storing stay. Only the rewritten linen count goes, and par-card upkeep is taken off. The low end is a site that never rewrites a count. The high end is a linen room that recopies the count onto a fresh sheet each delivery. Both sit under the central net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The cleaner still stocks carts, replenishes rooms and moves linen by hand. A few rewritten lists drop, and a second copy of the property report drops where the supervisor already accepts one note. The supervisor still accepts any report of damage, theft or a found article before it is filed.
reach: Housekeeping supervisors receive one property note, accepted by them, in place of a recopied report.
Laundry workers can read the closet par the cleaner counted, and still send linen the closet is short of.
skills_to_grow: Stock a cart from a par card without rewriting the list.
Write a property note that says what was seen and does not decide that a crime occurred.
Mark linen that should not go back into a room, and count it once on the closet card.
role.ambitious_version: Every cart, room type and linen closet shows its par on a card the cleaner can read while working, and a found article is with the supervisor before the room is prepared again. The cleaner still cleans, replenishes and moves linen by hand.
